questions.question: In the Bayesian approach, the unknown parameter θ is treated as...
options: A fixed constant with no uncertainty
A random quantity described by a probability distribution
The same as the sample mean
questions.explanation: Bayesians express uncertainty about a parameter with a probability distribution, which is updated as data arrive.

questions.question: Which statement matches a 95% credible interval of (22%, 51%)?
options: 95% of repeated studies would produce an interval containing θ
Given the data and prior, there is a 95% probability that θ lies between 22% and 51%
questions.explanation: A credible interval is a direct probability statement about the parameter, given the data and the prior.

questions.question: Prior Beta(1, 1), data: 14 successes in 40 trials. What is the posterior?
questions.explanation: Posterior = Beta(a + k, b + n − k) = Beta(1 + 14, 1 + 26) = Beta(15, 27).

questions.question: What is the mean of a Beta(15, 27) posterior?
The one-sided p-value is 0.072, and the posterior probability that θ > 25% is 93%. Which statement is true?
options: The p-value is P(data this extreme | θ = 25%), the posterior is P(θ > 25% | data): different questions
The posterior is not a probability
questions.explanation: One conditions on θ and asks about data, the other conditions on the data and asks about θ. They happen to be nearly complementary here because the prior is flat.

questions.question: With the same 14 of 40, a sceptical prior gives P(θ > 25%) = 87% and an optimistic one gives 99%. What does this tell you?
options: With little data, the prior has a noticeable effect, so check prior sensitivity
You must always use the flat prior
questions.explanation: With a small sample the prior still influences the posterior. Good practice is to state the prior and see how much conclusions change.

questions.question: What happens to the influence of the prior as the sample grows (same observed rate)?
options: It fades; different priors converge to similar posteriors
questions.explanation: With 400 customers all three priors in the lesson gave posterior means within one point of each other. Data overwhelm the prior.

questions.question: What is MCMC used for?
options: Drawing samples from a posterior distribution that has no simple formula
questions.explanation: MCMC builds a chain of parameter values whose long-run distribution is the posterior, so you can summarise any posterior from the draws.
